description: Real ext4, btrfs and fuse mounts (loop devices and a daemonless fuse mount) with df and btrfs shims first on the root PATH setting the numbers. Usage at 89%, 90% and 91% against the default 90% threshold gives OK, alert and alert. A threshold of 100 or abc is refused with exit 1. Btrfs metadata at 90% alerts with 0.5 GB unallocated and is OK with 10 GB. A fuse mount is named in the status under usrUnknownFs warn, alerts under alert and is hidden under ignore. TERM mid-run still prints one fallback result block, within 5 seconds.

steps.label: Fixtures: ext4, btrfs and fuse mounts under /mnt/tc-*, df and btrfs shims in /usr/local/sbin
89% used, threshold 90: OK
outputContains: STATUS=OK - 1 filesystem(s) checked, none at or above 90% used (no free-space floor set); fullest is /mnt/tc-ext4 at 89%

steps.label: 90% used, threshold 90: alert (at the threshold counts)
Threshold 100 is refused
outputContains: STATUS=Check could not run: usrThreshold must be between 1 and 99 (given: 100)

steps.label: Threshold abc is refused
outputContains: STATUS=Check could not run: usrThreshold must be a whole number 1-99 (given: 'abc')

steps.label: Btrfs metadata 90% (pool threshold 85) with 0.5 GB unallocated: alert, though df shows 50%
outputContains: STATUS=ALERT - /mnt/tc-btrfs (btrfs) metadata 90% full with only 0.5 GB unallocated

steps.label: Btrfs metadata 90% with 10 GB unallocated: OK, and verified
Unknown filesystem, usrUnknownFs warn (default): named in the status, exit 0
Unknown filesystem, usrUnknownFs alert: alert
outputContains: STATUS=ALERT - 1 mount(s) are a filesystem type this monitor cannot measure; 1 filesystem(s) checked

steps.label: Unknown filesystem, usrUnknownFs ignore: not mentioned, exit 0
TERM mid-run (df hanging): one fallback result block at once, saying it was stopped by a signal; the job ends 143
outputContains: STATUS=Check failed before it could measure anything (stopped by a signal)
start markers: 1, end markers: 1, STATUS lines: 1

steps.label: Clean up: shims and test mounts removed
